steps.description: Load /eval-four-arms-without-confounded-batch-n6-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, raw integer salmon counts, first column gene symbol) and /eval-four-arms-without-confounded-batch-n6-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition, batch). Verify and report the cross-tabulation of condition x batch, which is expected to be a perfect 6/6 diagonal (B1=control, B2=treated). Compute library sizes, detected-gene counts per sample, filter to genes with counts >= 10 in at least 6 samples, apply VST/rlog, and produce: PCA (PC1/PC2, points coloured by condition and shaped by batch — the two annotations will be identical), sample-sample correlation heatmap with hierarchical clustering, per-sample library-size barplot. Formally check design-matrix rank: build model.matrix(~batch+condition) and report that it is rank-deficient (number of columns vs rank), which is the algebraic statement of the confound. Write a short confound_assessment.md stating that condition and batch effects are non-identifiable in this design and that no statistical method can separate them.
acceptance_criteria: condition x batch contingency table written out and shown to be perfectly diagonal (6 control/B1, 6 treated/B2)
PCA plot, correlation heatmap and library-size plot saved as files
Rank check of model.matrix(~batch+condition) reported: number of coefficients and matrix rank, demonstrating deficiency
confound_assessment.md states explicitly that treatment and batch effects are non-identifiable and that batch correction cannot recover the treatment effect
Per-sample QC table (library size, genes detected) saved as CSV

caveats: A large DE gene count here is not evidence of a strong treatment effect; batch effects in RNA-seq routinely produce thousands of significant genes
p-value histogram shape (heavily anti-conservative) may itself indicate a strong technical component, but cannot distinguish it from a strong biological one
n=6 vs 6 gives limited power for modest effects even setting the confound aside
steps.context: This is the analysis the research question literally asks for. It is statistically valid as a two-group contrast; what it cannot do is attribute the difference to treatment. The plan runs it and constrains the interpretation rather than refusing.
steps.question: Which genes differ between the six treated (batch B2) and six control (batch B1) lung samples, under a design in which the estimated effect is treatment and batch combined?
constraints: Design must be ~condition only — do NOT add batch (the model is rank-deficient with both)
Do not apply ComBat, SVA, RUV or any other correction to the counts before DESeq2
Every output artefact must carry the confound caveat in its filename, header, or title
steps.description: Run DESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~condition, contrast treated vs control (control as reference level). Pre-filter to genes with count >= 10 in at least 6 samples. Use the default Wald test with independent filtering and BH FDR. Apply apeglm LFC shrinkage for ranking and reporting. Produce: full results table (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken LFC, stat, pvalue, padj) sorted by padj; counts of genes at padj<0.05 and |LFC|>1; MA plot; volcano plot; p-value histogram; heatmap of normalized VST values for the top 50 genes by padj annotated with BOTH condition and batch. CRITICAL LABELLING REQUIREMENT: name the results file and every column header/plot title so that the estimated effect is described as 'treated+B2 vs control+B1 (condition and batch confounded)', not as a treatment effect. Include a header comment block in the CSV and a short markdown note stating that these log2 fold changes are the sum of any treatment effect and any B2-vs-B1 processing effect and cannot be attributed to treatment.
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 results table for treated vs control written as CSV with shrunken LFCs, sorted by padj
Number of genes at padj<0.05, and at padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>1, reported
MA plot, volcano plot and p-value histogram saved
Top-50 heatmap annotated with condition AND batch tracks
Results file and accompanying note explicitly label the effect as a confounded condition+batch composite, with the words 'cannot be attributed to treatment' present

steps.name: Demonstrate why batch correction fails here
caveats: ComBat with a perfectly confounded batch will drive the between-group difference to approximately zero; this is arithmetic, not biology
sva may return zero surrogate variables or SVs perfectly correlated with condition; either outcome is the expected consequence of the confound
steps.context: Users frequently expect that a batch-correction step can rescue a confounded design. Showing the actual failure modes on this data is more convincing and more honest than a caveat sentence, and it forecloses a wrong re-analysis.
steps.question: What happens when standard batch-correction strategies (batch in the design, ComBat, surrogate variable analysis) are applied to a design where batch is perfectly confounded with condition, and how does that change the treated-vs-control result?
constraints: Do NOT present any output of this step as a corrected or de-confounded gene list — its purpose is diagnostic only
If a sub-analysis errors, record the error as the result rather than working around it
steps.description: Empirically demonstrate the non-identifiability, so the limitation is shown rather than asserted. Three sub-analyses, each reporting what happens and why: (1) attempt DESeq2 with design ~batch+condition and capture the resulting error/rank-deficiency message verbatim; (2) apply ComBat (sva package) to the VST matrix with batch as the batch variable and NO covariate model, then re-test treated vs control on the adjusted matrix with limma; report how many genes remain significant and state that this procedure removes the treatment effect by construction, so a near-zero result is an artefact of the method and not evidence of absence; (3) run sva/svaseq with mod=~condition and mod0=~1 and report the number of surrogate variables found and their correlation with condition — showing SVs either cannot be estimated or simply recapitulate the condition variable. Summarise in a short markdown table: method, what it estimates, why it is invalid here. Also compute and report the concordance (rank correlation and overlap of top-200 genes) between the T1S2 uncorrected result and the ComBat-adjusted result.
acceptance_criteria: The ~batch+condition rank-deficiency failure is reproduced and its message captured verbatim
ComBat-adjusted re-test is run and its DE gene count reported alongside the explicit statement that the correction removes the effect of interest by construction
sva/svaseq output reported: number of SVs and their correlation/confounding with the condition variable
Markdown summary table of method vs why-it-is-invalid written
Concordance between corrected and uncorrected results quantified (Spearman rho on the test statistic and top-200 overlap)

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on the composite ranking
caveats: Enrichment inherits the confound entirely — coherent biology in the results does not rule out a batch origin, since batches differ in RNA quality and library prep, which themselves produce coherent signatures (e.g. ribosomal, mitochondrial, stress-response sets)
GO BP sets are heavily nested; collapse redundant parent/child hits before reporting a count
steps.context: Enrichment here is interpretive support only. Because the input ranking is a condition+batch composite, no enriched pathway can be called treatment-responsive. Its usable value is the coherence diagnostic and a description of what the composite signal looks like.
steps.question: Do the genes ranked by the treated-vs-control (condition+batch confounded) statistic show coherent biological pathway structure, or does the signal look diffuse and technical?
constraints: Use human gene sets only — the data is Homo sapiens lung
Use the pre-ranked statistic over the whole tested gene list; do not run an over-representation test on an arbitrary padj cutoff list as the primary analysis
Do not describe any enriched pathway as a treatment response
steps.description: Take the full DESeq2 result from T1S2, rank all tested genes by the Wald statistic (or by -log10(p) * sign(LFC)), and run pre-ranked GSEA with fgsea against human gene sets: the MSigDB human hallmark collection and the MSigDB human GO Biological Process collection — both are available in the environment's reference store as HGNC-symbol GMT files; the counts matrix already uses gene symbols, so no ID conversion is needed beyond dropping unmatched symbols (report how many of the ~12,000 genes map). Use 10,000 permutations, min set size 15, max 500, BH FDR. Report the top enriched sets in each direction with NES and padj, a summary dot plot, and the leading-edge genes for the top sets. Additionally report a coherence diagnostic: the fraction of tested gene sets reaching padj<0.05, and whether the top sets cluster into a small number of related themes or are scattered — diffuse, theme-less enrichment across many unrelated sets is more consistent with a global technical shift than a targeted treatment response, though neither pattern is decisive. If either GMT collection is absent at run time, run with whichever is present and state which was missing; if both are absent, report the ranked gene list and skip enrichment rather than substituting an unrelated resource.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea run on the full ranked gene list against human hallmark and GO-BP symbol gene sets, with the number of symbols matched to each collection reported
Results table with NES, pvalue, padj, size and leading-edge genes written as CSV
Dot plot or barplot of top enriched sets in both directions saved
Coherence diagnostic reported: fraction of sets significant at padj<0.05 and a qualitative note on whether top sets form few related themes or are scattered
Every output states that the ranking reflects treatment and batch B2-vs-B1 jointly and that no set can be called treatment-responsive

plan.title: Treated vs control lung DE under confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human lung bulk RNA-seq samples (12,000 genes x 12 samples, raw salmon counts in counts.csv) with a metadata table carrying condition (6 treated, 6 control) and batch (B1 = all 6 controls, B2 = all 6 treated). Batch is perfectly confounded with condition: no model can separate a treatment effect from a processing-batch effect, and no batch-correction method (ComBat, SVA, RUV, adding batch to the design) can rescue it — adding batch to the design matrix makes it rank-deficient, and applying ComBat with condition as the covariate of interest removes exactly the effect being tested. The plan therefore does the only defensible thing: it (T1S1) demonstrates the confound explicitly on this data so the limitation is a documented result rather than an assertion; (T1S2) runs the standard DESeq2 ~condition contrast treated vs control, whose estimates are reported as condition+batch composite effects, never as treatment effects; (T1S3) shows what actually happens when batch correction is attempted, so readers see the rank-deficiency and the circularity rather than trusting a corrected table; and (T2S1) runs hallmark/GO enrichment on the ranked composite statistic with the same labelling caveat, since pathway coherence is weak evidence about whether the signal looks biological or technical. Every downstream artefact carries the caveat in its own header. No plan step claims to identify treatment-specific genes, because this design cannot.
